brief: SG's strategy note argues that although AAII sentiment has turned increasingly bearish and valuations have de-rated on Fed tightening, this is not a 'Big Top' because the shocks look bigger than the damage: wages have outpaced diesel prices since 2008, wage pressure is running at half its 2022 level with inflation reverting and Fed hawkishness peaking, a 10-year yield of 5.5% would only match the nominal GDP trend so credit events need a velocity shock rather than a yield level, and AI investment shows up as productivity (real sales per employee at all-time highs, seven of ten sectors rising) rather than speculation. SG's allocation is 60% stocks, 20% commodities, 20% fixed income, with an S&P 500 target of 8000 and upside to 10,000 on a hyperscaler free-cash inflection, hedged via long gold, CNH, JPY and Topix Banks against fiscal-sustainability risk. The note also lays out why the bull market eventually ends: valuations remain stretched versus bonds, Fed tightening cycles have ended in recession 11 of 14 times, greedflation could recur, and market breadth is deteriorating rapidly.
